issue.title: [RPP] min_distance_to_obstacle and velocity_scaled_lookahead dont work well together when min_lookahead < min_distance_to_obstacle
issue.body:
## Bug report

**Required Info:**

- Operating System:
    - Ubuntu 24.04
- Computer:
  - Intel Twin Lake N150, 8GB RAM
- ROS2 Version:
  - Jazzy installed via deb packages
- Version or commit hash:
  - 1.3.8-1noble.20250915.220228
  - Custom RPP with min_distance_to_obstacle from Rolling implemented
- DDS implementation:
  - Zenoh

#### Expected behavior

When using `min_distance_to_obstacle`, I would expect the robot to stop when an obstacle is detected within this range and remain stationary until the path is clear. The collision checking logic should consistently enforce this safety distance, even when the robot's velocity is zero.

#### Actual behavior

The robot initially stops correctly at the specified `min_distance_to_obstacle`. However, it then begins to slowly "creep" forward in a stop-and-go pattern, gradually getting closer to the obstacle and not maintaining the intended safety gap.
I've observed this same creeping pattern in two different scenarios:

1) When using a custom modification to the controller that commands zero velocity on imminent collision.
2) When using the default controller behavior that triggers a Wait recovery on the BT.

#### Steps to reproduce issue

1. Configure the RPP controller with the following parameters, ensuring `min_lookahead_dist` is smaller than `min_distance_to_obstacle`:

```yaml
use_collision_detection: true 
use_velocity_scaled_lookahead_dist: true
min_distance_to_obstacle: 0.65
min_lookahead_dist: 0.2 
```

2. Run a navigation task, and put an obstacle on the robot's path.

3. The robot will approach the obstacle, stop correctly at the `min_distance_to_obstacle`, but then slowly creep closer to it.

#### Additional information

In [isCollisionImminent](https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/blob/ed0d59ff8ffd72631620a1a81c60e2d69c0d14eb/nav2_regulated_pure_pursuit_controller/src/collision_checker.cpp#L114C1-L116), the simulation distance is limited by `carrot_dist`, which shrinks to `min_lookahead_dist` when stopped. This prevents the checker from evaluating the full `min_distance_to_obstacle` range.

```cpp
if (hypot(curr_pose.position.x - robot_xy.x, curr_pose.position.y - robot_xy.y) > carrot_dist) {
    break;
}
```

 **A potential fix that I've tested locally:**

To ensure the simulation always respects the safety margin, the distance boundary can be modified to account for `min_distance_to_obstacle`. This can be done by defining a new limit before the loop:

```cpp
double simulation_distance_limit = std::max(carrot_dist, params_->min_distance_to_obstacle);
```

And updating the break condition to use this new limit:
```cpp
if (hypot(curr_pose.x - robot_xy.x, curr_pose.y - robot_xy.y) > simulation_distance_limit) {
    break;
}
```

This change was tested on a physical robot and resolved the creeping behavior, with no observed negative side effects on general navigation.

I'm opening this issue to report the behavior and share my findings. I'm not sure if the current interaction is the intended design, but this approach seems to make the feature more reliable. I'm curious to hear your thoughts.

comments.body:
> When using a custom modification to the controller that commands zero velocity on imminent collision.

Is that not in RPP already? If not, can you please open a PR to add that if you found a gap?

---

> the distance boundary can be modified to account for min_distance_to_obstacle

That seems reasonable, but would you think it would also be reasonable to say that the `min_distance_to_obstacle` must be greater than or equal to the minimum lookahead distance? If we say this, we can check this on Configuration / Dynamic Configuration and throw an exception or reject the dynamic update if violated. 

Do you want to have the minimum distance smaller than the minimum lookahead? 

@doisyg this is related to something you added - FYI. Any feedback you want to provide?

comments.body:
Thanks for the quick reply!

> Is that not in RPP already? If not, can you please open a PR to add that if you found a gap?

My bad, I phrased that poorly. By default RPP throws an exception, which is fine. For our specific use case, we wanted the robot to just stop and wait if it encounters an obstacle. Since in the BT we were basically just triggering thw wait recovery and calling RPP again, I thought it was reasonable to make a local modification for it to just publish a zero velocity instead of throwing an exception.

What I meant is that I observed this "creeping" behavior regardless of how the robot was stopped, whether by my zero velocity modification or by the default using the wait recovery.

> Do you want to have the minimum distance smaller than the minimum lookahead?

I want to have min_distance greater than the min lookahead (in other words, min_lookahead must be smaller than min_distance). 

Basically, I want RPP to stop with a safety margin (like 0.6m - 1.0m), and for that, min_distance seems appropriated. At the same time, I need to keep min_lookahead small, because if I increase it too much, the robot starts to cut corners excessively.

I'm not sure if this is the intended use for the parameter. I'm kind of new to navigation, so please take this with a pinch of salt. Based on my use case, a constraint like this:

> but would you think it would also be reasonable to say that the min_distance_to_obstacle must be greater than or equal to the minimum lookahead distance? 

would actually be problematic, as I would have to choose between having this safety margin or a good path tracking. It seems difficult to achieve both with that constraint.
